title: Remove obsolete flat Settings WebView exports
summary: Removed the four remaining transitional flat exports from settingsView.js and migrated all identified runtime, browser-smoke, static-contract, and Tauri contract consumers to window.mediaPipelineSettingsView. The Settings namespace remains the sole cross-module API for these functions, and the authoritative inventory now reports 375 flat exports across 48 files.
reason: Complete one bounded Settings-domain cleanup slice after proving each alias had an existing namespace replacement and enumerating every direct consumer and DOM reference before removal.
behavior_before: settingsView.js published renderSettingsRawActionPlan, renderSettings, getLastSettings, and initSettingsViewEvents both through mediaPipelineSettingsView and as flat window aliases. App orchestration, cross-page settings access, launch, rename, library-profile helpers, and browser/static fixtures still consumed those flat aliases.
behavior_after: The same functions remain available through window.mediaPipelineSettingsView only. All identified consumers and test fixtures use namespace-first access; no inline DOM handlers referenced the aliases, and backend-owned routes, settings persistence, media policy, confirmations, and command semantics are unchanged.
manual_validation: Proof scan found no remaining selected flat Settings assignments/consumers outside negative assertions and no matching inline HTML handlers.
npm run webview:check passed across all WebView assets.
Targeted ESLint on the nine affected WebView runtime files completed with zero errors; current workspace warnings come from concurrent split work.
Targeted Settings namespace static test, WebView inventory tests (5), rename-readiness smoke, and Tauri served-WebView contract test passed.
WebView map, public-contract, split-candidate, and script-order checks passed; script-order loaded 282 scripts and verified mediaPipelineSettingsView.
Scoped refresh_summaries completed for affected sources, tests, and inventory.

Full webview:prework:check passed JavaScript syntax checking, then failed the shared ESLint warning budget because concurrent unrelated WebView split work increased repository-wide warnings/errors. DOM-gap, route-ownership, and command-boundary checks also remain stale/failing on unrelated current-workspace changes.

Additional LibraryProfiles, Rename, and Diagnostics browser suites were attempted; unrelated fixture/helper failures prevented them from passing, while the required Settings/Launch browser smoke passed.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet's Settings consumer, fixture, inventory, and namespace-export changes; restore the four flat settingsView.js assignments; then refresh the WebView contract artifacts and generated summaries.
notes: Python impact: test expectations and browser fixtures only; no Python runtime API or backend route changed. Removed flat aliases: renderSettingsRawActionPlan, renderSettings, getLastSettings, initSettingsViewEvents. Retained namespace functions: mediaPipelineSettingsView.renderSettingsRawActionPlan, mediaPipelineSettingsView.renderSettings, mediaPipelineSettingsView.getLastSettings, mediaPipelineSettingsView.initSettingsViewEvents. Retained Settings split-child stashes (__settingsRawTriageModule, __settingsSafetyLocksModule, and builder-module stashes) because parents consume and delete them during script load. All non-Settings flat exports remain outside this bounded cleanup. The browser smoke now retries its real designation change event until the delegated application handler is installed, eliminating a DOMContentLoaded startup race without bypassing handler verification. Shared generated WebView map/contract/slice files were refreshed against a concurrently changing worktree and intentionally not absorbed into this packet.
